name: Queen Victoria Market
desc: A city block of cheese, doughnuts and bargain fruit under heritage sheds since 1878. Sample your way to full.

name: Hosier Lane
desc: The famous ever-changing graffiti lane — new masterpieces sprayed over old ones weekly. Free gallery, open 24/7.

name: Royal Botanic Gardens
desc: 38 hectares of lakes, lawns and black swans one tram-hop from the CBD. Nature's free co-working space.

name: Federation Square
desc: The angular plaza everyone loves to argue about — big screens, buskers, free wifi and prime people-watching by the Yarra.

name: St Kilda Pier Penguins
desc: Wild little penguins waddle home to the breakwater at dusk. A zero-dollar wildlife documentary, filmed live nightly.

name: Melbourne Cricket Ground
desc: The 100,000-seat cathedral of sport. Tour the hallowed turf, or just soak up the roar from outside on game day.

name: National Gallery of Victoria
desc: Australia's oldest gallery, water-wall entrance included. The permanent collection costs exactly nothing.

name: Melbourne Skydeck
desc: 88 floors up with the whole glittering grid of Melbourne stretching to the horizon. Save it for a payday sunset.

name: Luna Park
desc: A 1912 seaside fair you enter through a giant grinning mouth. Wandering in is free; the heritage rides are the splurge.

name: Flinders Street Station
desc: The mustard-yellow station with the domed clocks — 'meet me under the clocks' is a whole Melbourne love language. Free.
